title: Ports and connectors: USB, HDMI, DisplayPort, Ethernet and audio

videos.script: The last lesson was the five things you touch. This one is how they get in. {{in}} A port is three separate promises wearing one shape: the plug that fits, the protocol that runs over it, and the speed that protocol is running at. All three can disagree, and the connector tells you about exactly one of them. {{three}} That is the whole difficulty, and USB is where it is worst. A socket shaped like a USB-C can be carrying anything from four hundred and eighty megabits to forty gigabits, may or may not charge a laptop, and may or may not drive a monitor. Nothing on the outside says which. {{usb}} Video is a smaller mess with the same shape. Networking is the one place where the numbers are honest. And the audio jack is the oldest connector here by about sixty years and still the one people put in the wrong hole. {{rest}} We finish on the back of a machine with the names taken off, because knowing what a socket is by looking at it is the point of all of this.
